heroHeadline: Milo Yiannopoulos Deported by ICE as August Arrests Hit Third Straight Monthly Record of 50,925
heroSubtitle: DHS announced Sept 2, 2026 that ICE arrested 50,925 people in August, the third consecutive monthly record and the second month over 50,000, with more than 300,000 arrests logged in 2026 to date. The same week, Chinese national Lianyong Wei, 51, died hours after intake at ICE's Saipan facility on Aug 23 — the 57th detainee death since Trump's second term began — prompting a formal protest from China's government demanding an investigation. An unnamed ICE enforcement surge that began around Indianapolis on Aug 31 drew a formal congressional inquiry from Rep. André Carson on Sept 3 after Mayor Joe Hogsett said his office received no federal notice of the operation, while evening protests gathered outside a hotel believed to house the agents involved. In New York, DHS touted the conclusion of 'Operation Rotten Apple,' a five-week surge that netted 2,197 arrests across the state, and on Sept 4 students at more than 100 Colorado schools staged a statewide walkout protesting ICE's presence in their communities. The 287(g) program remains expanded to roughly 2,179+ active agreements, and ICE's FY2026 detention death toll stays elevated with Acting Director Venturella's June 4 memo ending post-release death reporting still in effect.
